# uicp

> Headless drawer / sheet / nav primitives for vanilla JS and Svelte. ~8.6 KB brotlied total (core + adapter + gesture). You own all the CSS.

uicp is a small, opinionated library targeting **static sites, marketing pages, and tiny widgets** that want modern drawer UX without pulling in a framework runtime. The adapter only sets DOM state hooks (data-attrs, ARIA, classes); the user writes every line of CSS for position, transform, and transition.

Not a Radix/Vaul competitor for React-heavy apps. A complement to them for vanilla / static / non-framework contexts.

## Quick start

- [README.md](readme.md): Install, basic usage, framework adapters, bundle sizes
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): Version history with breaking changes (v0.4.0 is the first real npm release)
- [LICENSE](LICENSE): MIT

## Examples (runnable)

Run `python3 -m http.server 8088` from repo root, then:

- [examples/tiny-html/](examples/tiny-html/): 3-direction drawer (bottom / right / left) edge-to-edge style, vanilla HTML + Tailwind CDN
- [examples/homelog-gatepass/](examples/homelog-gatepass/): iOS-17 floating sheet pattern, Wallet-style Pass switcher, mobile-first

Both demos are also documented in [examples/README.md](examples/README.md).

## State hooks (write your CSS against these)

The adapter sets these on the drawer element:

- `data-uip-type="drawer"`
- `data-uip-position="left" | "right" | "top" | "bottom"`
- `data-uip-open="true" | "false"`
- `aria-hidden="true" | "false"`
- class `.uip-open` / `.uip-closed`

Backdrop (provide via `<div data-backdrop-for="drawer-id">`):

- class `.uip-backdrop-open`
- `data-uip-open="true" | "false"`

## Package surface (npm)

- `@nature-labs/uicp-core` — primitives + state machine
- `@nature-labs/uicp-adapter-vanilla` — vanilla JS bindings
- `@nature-labs/uicp-adapter-svelte` — Svelte store + action
- `@nature-labs/uicp-plugin-gesture` — touch swipe-to-close
- `@nature-labs/uicp-plugin-snap` — snap points
- `@nature-labs/uicp-plugin-direction` — RTL/LTR

Not yet shipped (don't reference these as if they exist):
- React / Vue / Solid / Web Components adapters
- Animation plugin with physics
- Modal/popover/tooltip/menu wrappers in vanilla adapter (only `drawer` is wired through)
